hero.title: A fabrication shop for the whole region.
hero.subtitle: GEarheads run a full-service Production Hub, machining custom parts for FTC teams across the region who lack the equipment, expertise, or time to fabricate on their own. CNC milling, 3D printing, laser cutting, plotter printing — if you need it made, we make it.

heroPhoto.caption: Production Hub fabrication space — mills and printers running

impact.label: Why it matters
impact.text: 26 FTC teams call this ecosystem home in 2026. Most of them are rookies or small programs that cannot afford a CNC mill or spend weeks learning manufacturing from scratch. The Production Hub closes that gap: any team can submit a design and receive a finished part, letting them focus on what they do best — building competitive robots and learning engineering skills — rather than being blocked by fabrication constraints.

howItWorks.label: How It Works
howItWorks.heading: From design file to finished part

inlinePhoto.caption: GEarheads manufacturing subteam — mid-run on the industrial mill

howItWorks.body:
A team reaches out — usually via our group chat, a direct message from a mentor, or a conversation at a qualifier. They share their design file: an Onshape link, a DXF export, an STL, or sometimes a rough sketch in a shared doc. From there, our manufacturing subteam takes over. The student who owns the request reviews the geometry for tool-path feasibility, confirms material and tolerances with the requesting team, and gets it into the queue. That feedback loop — before a single cut is made — is where most fitment problems get caught.

Fabrication runs on our shop schedule. During the build season that can mean evenings and weekend sessions; in the off-season we batch jobs more loosely. For CNC work, our team handles all CAM setup so the requesting team never needs to touch G-code. For 3D prints, we orient, support, and monitor each job. For laser work, we confirm the geometry converts cleanly from vector before committing sheet material. When a part comes off the machine, a second student checks it against the design spec before it goes into a handoff bag.

Delivery happens at the next shared event — a practice session, qualifier, or a dedicated pickup at our shop. For teams that are farther away, we have shipped parts. The whole cycle, from intake message to part-in-hand, typically runs three to ten days depending on queue depth and complexity. Teams that have gone through the process once know exactly what to expect the second time — and many come back every season.

services.title: CNC Milling
services.description: GEarheads operate three CNC mills in-house: a custom-built MPCNC (Mostly Printed CNC) designed and assembled by the team, a 6×6 industrial-grade mill capable of handling full robot-size sheet stock, and a large-format PrintNC for high-throughput plate work. Teams submit their Onshape or DXF files and our manufacturing subteam handles everything from CAM setup to final cut. We mill aluminum, polycarbonate, HDPE, and plywood — the same material stack we use on our own competition robots. Because we design-to-tolerance and run quality checks after every cut, the parts that leave our shop are ready to install, not ready to be re-drilled. For a rookie team that has never run a CNC machine, receiving a precision-milled drivetrain plate or intake arm can be the difference between a robot that works and one that shakes apart at the first match. We do not just hand off parts — we talk through the geometry with the requesting team, flag any wall-thickness issues we see in their CAD, and suggest fixes before material is touched. Over a season, that mentorship layer compounds: teams that start by receiving parts end up understanding tolerances, feeds-and-speeds, and DFM principles they would not have encountered otherwise.
highlights: Three mills on-site: custom MPCNC, 6×6 industrial mill, large-format PrintNC
Cuts aluminum, polycarbonate, HDPE, and plywood
Accepts Onshape links and DXF/SVG exports directly
CAM setup handled by GEarheads — no G-code knowledge required
Post-cut quality checks before every delivery
Design feedback included — wall-thickness, fit, and DFM notes on every job

services.title: 3D Printing
services.description: FDM 3D printing is the fastest path from a CAD sketch to a working prototype, and GEarheads have dialed in the process across PLA, PETG, and TPU. We print brackets, motor mounts, sensor housings, guide channels, and any geometry that would be impossible or impractical to mill. Teams submit STL or 3MF files and we handle slicing, orientation, support strategy, and print monitoring. Parts are inspected for layer adhesion and dimensional accuracy before handoff. We can also iterate: if the first print reveals a fit issue, we discuss the fix, reslice, and reprint typically within a day. This tight feedback loop is how teams learn design-for-manufacturability without expensive trial-and-error on their own machines.
highlights: PLA, PETG, and TPU in stock
Prints brackets, mounts, housings, channels, and complex geometry
Slicing and support strategy handled by GEarheads
Dimensional inspection on every part before delivery
Fast iteration cycle — typically same-day re-prints on fit fixes

services.title: Laser Cutting
services.description: Laser cutting unlocks a different material world than CNC milling: thin sheet acrylic, Delrin, wood, fabric, and foam can be cut to tight tolerances without tooling pressure that would warp or crack the workpiece. GEarheads use their laser cutter to produce robot field elements, bumper guides, wire management panels, and decorative robot shells for teams that want a clean, professional look at competition. The laser is also the right tool for etching team numbers, part labels, and sponsor logos directly into panels — a detail that impresses judges and drives awards consideration. We accept SVG and DXF geometry and can convert raster artwork to vector paths if a team only has a logo file.
highlights: Cuts acrylic, Delrin, wood, foam, and thin sheet material
Accepts SVG and DXF; raster-to-vector conversion available
Etches logos, team numbers, and part labels directly into panels
Clean-cut edges ready for direct installation
Useful for field elements, wire panels, and robot cosmetics

services.title: Plotter Printing
services.description: A competition robot that is well-documented and visually polished signals to judges that the team takes their work seriously. GEarheads' vinyl plotter and large-format printer produce team graphics, robot decals, engineering portfolio covers, and pit signage at competition quality. We help teams translate their branding into a coherent visual identity — logo sizing, color matching, material selection for durability under field conditions — and output finished vinyl cuts or prints ready to apply. This matters more than many rookie teams realize: Inspire Award evaluations factor in how a team presents their work, and a clean, professional pit setup with matching graphics and a well-laid-out portfolio signals the same level of organization that judges look for in every other category. We have produced graphics for teams with zero design experience and helped them look like they have been at this for years.
highlights: Vinyl cuts and large-format prints for robot decals and pit signage
Logo sizing, color matching, and material selection guidance
Durability-rated materials for field and transportation conditions
Engineering portfolio covers and presentation inserts
Helps rookie teams present at competition quality from day one

partners.name: Pack-a-Punch
partners.description: One of the first teams to receive Production Hub support, Pack-a-Punch brought us a drivetrain plate design that needed precision holes and weight-reduction pockets their shop couldn't run. We milled their aluminum plates on the industrial mill and helped them work through their CAD tolerances so the final assembly fit clean.

partners.name: Random Engineers
partners.description: The Random Engineers came to us mid-season with a custom intake arm that wasn't available off the shelf in the geometry they needed. We 3D-printed multiple iterations across two days, dialing in the angle and clearance until it ran without hitting the robot frame at any extension point.

partners.name: Tundrabots
partners.description: Tundrabots needed laser-cut field element panels for their practice setup — dimensions that matched the official game elements without the cost of buying a second kit. We cut and handed off panels within a week of receiving their measurements, letting them run full-field practice while their regional peers were still doing dry runs on partial setups.

partners.name: Hapabots
partners.description: We've worked with Hapabots across multiple seasons, from early plotter-printed robot graphics that helped them look polished at their first qualifier, to later support getting their own X-Carve CNC machine configured and running. Hapabots are now part of our DIY-CNC initiative — moving from Production Hub recipients to self-sufficient fabricators.
